subject.measured_quantity: provider-reported token usage of an AI agent completing an accepted equivalent repository task
subject.interpretation: AIT and Git do not intrinsically consume model tokens; this protocol compares declared agent workflow surfaces.

core.topology: one fresh single-agent session per run

modes.repository_surface: real Git working tree without .ait metadata
modes.required_evidence: task-relevant explicit Git discovery, status, history, or diff commands
modes.metadata_isolation: runner-owned writable Git metadata is outside the Codex-protected candidate root and inherited through standard GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE; candidate commands must not override or redirect it

modes.repository_surface: current solo_local sprint-off AIT Task, Snapshot, inspection, and local-land workflow
modes.required_evidence: effective solo_local sprint-off authority plus task-relevant local AIT workflow commands without Plan binding, raw Git, or ait-server substitution

mode.repository_surface: one fresh AIT linear session with one benchmark-owned compact execution brief
mode.claim_boundary: benchmark context experiment; it does not change the current AIT product workflow

brief_constraints: derived from the shared task contract
contains no solution or file-location hint absent from shared inputs
generation cost is counted in first-use or precomputed symmetrically in steady-state

first_use_total_cost.repository_identity_policy: both modes pin benchmark-agent identity inside the fresh repository before the baseline revision

workloads.name: projectile-cooldown-regression
workloads.required_outcome: diagnose and repair a seeded rapid-fire or cooldown defect without unrelated gameplay changes

workloads.name: armored-enemy-feature
workloads.required_outcome: add a deterministic two-hit enemy, score rule, original visual distinction, and tests

workloads.name: replay-divergence-diagnosis
workloads.required_outcome: repair seeded replay divergence after pause and resume

workloads.name: gameplay-modularization
workloads.required_outcome: split a monolithic gameplay implementation while preserving exact observable behavior

workloads.name: beta-release-hardening
workloads.required_outcome: add replay persistence, settings schema, mobile input, focus recovery, benchmark UI, validation, and release documentation

fixture_contract.tracked_content_equivalence: byte-equivalent content digest for every paired mode in one comparison cell
required_properties: original local HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and assets
no backend or external network dependency
machine-readable input, event-log, observable-state, startup, and validation contracts

provider_usage.authority: provider-reported machine-readable session log or API response
provider_usage.provider_session_failure_policy: retain the invalid pre-execution run and stop the remaining schedule immediately

primary_metrics.effective_tokens_per_accepted_task: sum(provider_total_tokens for every valid attempted run) / count(accepted equivalent outcomes)

fairness.project_document_loading: disabled symmetrically with project_doc_max_bytes=0; mode rules come only from the frozen measured prompt
fairness.git_metadata_layout: isolated external writable directory supplied to the Codex sandbox and used by runner bootstrap, candidate commands, and closeout verification

sampling.aggregate_method: median of paired workload and run ratios

invalid_run_conditions: paired tracked content or task prompt differs
model, reasoning effort, tools, cache, or network policy drifted
Git mode lacks explicit Git repository discovery evidence
Git mode overrides or redirects the runner-owned repository metadata context
AIT mode lacks current AIT workflow evidence
AIT mode contacted ait-server or any remote AIT authority
excluded topology entered only one core mode
provider usage is missing or ambiguous
provider session failed before candidate execution
mandatory acceptance failed or human repair occurred
failed or high-token attempts were discarded

claim_eligibility.scope: game-development workloads, pinned model, declared profile, and declared topology only

non_goals: claim AIT always uses fewer tokens than Git
claim AIT is faster or cheaper for every repository task
compare different model providers inside one AIT-versus-Git claim
generalize game-development results to unrelated domains
treat token savings alone as developer productivity
